production.note: US model years 2001 to 2003, the years rated 550 hp. Classic.com: 'The Saleen S7 was a high performance supercar that was launched in 2000 for the 2001 model year' (and 'produced for model years 2001 to 2009' across all versions). Cars.com: 'In 2001, Saleen began to ease into the production-car arena with the mid-engine S7.' (carscom-s7-2004). Excluded: the 2004 model year, for which Cars.com reports 'engine output gets a boost to 575 hp and 570 pounds-feet of torque' (announced at the 2004 Chicago Auto Show), and the 2005-on S7 Twin Turbo (duPont Registry: 'the S7 gained twin turbos in 2005', dupont-s7). The race S7-R is separate. No opened page states 2003 as the last 550 hp model year in so many words; it follows from the 2004 rating change.

displacementL.note: About 6,997 cc (427 cu in). Saleen: '7.0L'; Sports Car Digest: 'increased its displacement to 427 cubic inches' (sportscardigest-s7-2003). No cc figure was seen on a qualifying page; 427 cu in x 16.387 = 6,997 cc, rounded to 7.0 either way.

fuel.note: Petrol V8; inferred from the description.

drivetrain.note: Cars.com: 'A six-speed-manual transmission drives the rear wheels.'

transmission.note: Cars.com: 'A six-speed-manual transmission drives the rear wheels.' Sports Car Digest: 'Six-speed manual transaxle and limited-slip differential' (sportscardigest-s7-2003).

powerHp.note: Quote (Saleen): "Initially powered by a Saleen-designed 7.0L naturally aspirated V8 that delivers 550 horsepower and 520 lb-ft of torque, the S7 launches from 0 to 60 in under four seconds and can exceed 200 mph." (reproduced on a second request). Cars.com: 'the fully re-engineered engine produced 550 horsepower.' (carscom-s7-2004); duPont Registry: 'This last great triumph of the Windsor block made 550 hp naturally aspirated.' (dupont-s7). The 575 hp 2004 model year is excluded from this record (see production note).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (single named-author article; figure not tied to a model year). Quote (duPont Registry, Andrew Nabors, 5 August 2016): "At 160 mph, the carbon fiber body creates the supercar's 2,750 lb curb weight in downforce..." (reproduced on a second request). Cars.com Editors (unbylined, 2004 and 2005 model-year articles, i.e. years outside this record): 'The S7 weighs approximately 2,750 pounds.' (carscom-s7-2004), corroboration only. Saleen's current S7 page shows an unlabelled spec block with '2,800 lbs Curb Weight' beside '750 hp Max Horsepower (Twin-Turbo)'; it does not say which version it describes and is probably the Twin Turbo's (saleen-s7-page), 1.8% higher; not used. Unattributed tables (Supercars.net 'Editorial Team', HotCars) print '2756 lbs' / 1,250 kg and are not used. Six-speed manual, the only gearbox.

sources.title: The Saleen S7: America's First Production Supercar

provisionalNote: Weight (2,750 lb) rests on a single named-author article (duPont Registry, Andrew Nabors) that does not tie the figure to a model year or engine, with Cars.com's unbylined 'approximately 2,750 pounds' agreeing. Power (550 hp) is Saleen's own figure. A Saleen press kit or brochure, or a Car and Driver / Road & Track / MotorTrend spec panel for a 2001-2003 S7, giving a curb weight would replace it.
